correctness.rationale: The finite selection identity reduces the centered strong Hilbert norm exactly to 4096 singular values. The embedded stdlib program calculates all 4096 integer Gram matrices, proving by exact Sylvester/Bareiss arithmetic that 4084 are strictly below the rational squared threshold \(1517/1000\); all 12 exceptional matrices are one dihedral orbit. Exact LeVerrier coefficients give the quintic characteristic factor; Descartes signs isolate its unique root above the threshold; rational interval arithmetic certifies an exact positive polynomial eigenvector and 18 strict active-ball inequalities. Perron simplicity yields all 12 nonnegative equality rays. The package contains full source and exact replay commands.

originality.rationale: The exact centered strong \(\ell^2\) norm and full 12-ray equality classification for the unweighted six-cycle are not implied by the inspected 2014 general graph-maximal bounds, the 2020 complete/star Hilbert results, or the 2026 finite-graph variation results. Targeted public-record and algebraic-coefficient searches uncovered no equivalent claim. Local exact computations for \(C_4\) and \(C_5\), and variation bounds for \(C_6\), concern different graphs or invariants; the six-cycle has four ball radii, and neither a monotonicity theorem nor a formula applying to all cycles was located. This is qualified best-knowledge originality, not absolute priority.

value.rationale: The six-cycle is the smallest cycle with four distinct centered ball radii and diameter three, a natural new analytic regime beyond the three-ball four- and five-cycle cases. The exact quintic spectral invariant not implied by inspected prior theorems and complete twelve-ray symmetry classification describe an intrinsic sharp operator norm, with a reproducible boundary benchmark for larger even-cycle maximal inequalities. The claim is not merely a numerical sample or arbitrary weighted slice.
